citations.quote: QuickSAT, and the supporting database environment step_SATdb, is a collaborative Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) environment for application in a range of space vehicles including CubeSATs through 1000+ kg class satellites for orbits in Earth and missions throughout the solar system.

The objectives of UNP are to educate and train the future workforce through a national student satellite design and fabrication competition and to enable small satellite R&D, payload development, integration and flight test, Air Force related technologies.

The current program, NS-7, has two distinct stages. The first part is a nanosat design and protoflight build phase, which lasts approximately two years and culminates in the AIAA Student Satellite Flight Competition Review (FCR).

This second phase consists of integration with the Lightband/P-POD and environmental testing of the flight Nanosat at AFRL in the summer of 2014 in preparation for a potential flight made available through STP, per the outcome of the DoD Space Experiments Review Board (SERB) flight request process. The Program Office will assist the winning university in testing, any necessary
step_SATdb allows for the exchange of data between existing design tools such as MATLAB, SINDA, SOAP and QuickSAT

The key advantage of the step_SATdb for the U.S. Government, universities and the aerospace industry is that the data architecture is open source and can be implemented using a range of database environments including MySQL, Oracle or MS SQL to name a few.

A configuration stores the physical configuration of a satellite - system components and subsystems, component location and orientation within a satellite, launch vehicle information and power and propulsion elements at the satellite level.

Each revision maintains a flight plan that defines all flight legs and phases of flight plus the modes of operation and the active modes of operation for each flight leg. Each flight leg then tracks to a set of analysis tools - internal and external. This includes link analysis, power analysis, thermal analysis, ACDS, and orbit modeling to name a few.
Currently, eleven teams in the UNP-7 are using the QuickSAT/step_SATdb environment.

- Master Equipment List development and tracking

- Flight planning

- Flight mode definition

- Part definition

- Launch vehicle selection

Students were optionally allowed to use other tools within the QuickSAT environment including the following modules: Link Analysis, Propulsion Analysis, Thermal Analysis, Attitude Control and Determination, Orbit Modeling (via the SOAP interface tool), Power Analysis and the report functions.
In addition to the UNP student teams, several reviewers, monitors and AFRL and UNP program managers had access to QuickSAT/step_SATdb to review each student team's data, design and progress.
For EP systems, the user would separately track the power bounds within the power module.

The QuickSAT/step_SATdb PLM environment stores and distributes the supporting satellite design, configuration, mission, manufacturing and test data from a centralized database/cloud environment and can distribute the data across multiple platforms and via the internet.

This exercise by the student teams also served to help the developer of QuickSAT-sciZone to understand how QuickSAT is being utilized, find any bugs missed in the testing process and to determine areas of improvement.
